single_player_reachability.question: which kinds the executable must be able to build locally for a single-player mission
single_player_reachability.answer: 30 of the 34 armed kinds have a construction site inside a defined Ghidra function, so a local session needs almost the whole table rather than a network-only subset. Ten of the 30 are reached from a Lua binding, which is what a mission script drives. None of the 34 is network-only in the sense of having no local construction site at all except 6Ch and 98h, whose kind bytes are computed rather than pushed.

producer_in_undefined_code.91h: 008144A0, a unit virtual at slot 23Ch in nine vtables. The producer is identified; the callers of slot 23Ch were not enumerated.
producer_in_undefined_code.9Dh: 009D6650. No reference of any kind resolves into it, so the trigger is unresolved.

single_player_reachability.method: the base constructor 0075B430 stores its one stack argument at msg+10h, so scanning .text for the last PUSH imm before a CALL to 0075B430 names the kind at every direct construction site: 426 sites, 25 of which compute the kind. Containing functions came from the live Ghidra bodies via tools/verify_report_calls.py, not from the index's nearest-start approximation, which is what exposed the six undefined-code sites.
single_player_reachability.caveat: A linear byte scan for callers of the five unreferenced constructors is not proof of absence: it resyncs from arbitrary offsets and cannot establish provenance. The claim here is that no CALL rel32 and no aligned dword pointer in any section resolves into those ranges, not that the game never builds those kinds.

flow_gap_check: both listings were paged in full and checked for holes: 00821E80 has 411 consecutive instructions from 00821E80 to 00822391 and 0095ABE0 has 177 from 0095ABE0 to 0095AE1D, with no step above 10 bytes. The 9Dh arm's `_free`-class call at 0082232D (004404F0) and the string free at 0095AD63 (0041DD20) are both followed by listed instructions, so neither produced a dropped run.

corrections.was: `0095ABE0`'s own switch covers `4Bh`, `4Ch`, `79h`, `7Dh`-`80h` and returns false for the rest (`0095AE06`).
corrections.is: the kind list is right, but 0095AE06 is not a false return: it calls 00878350(this, msg) with ECX = this and returns that callee's result. 00878350 answers 4Bh, 4Ch, 56h MT_DAMAGEDGFXLEVEL and D2h with 1, and only its own default returns 0. A caller of vtable[164h] therefore sees true for three more kinds than the two switches alone explain.
corrections.evidence: 0095AE06 PUSH EAX / 0095AE07 MOV ECX,ESI / 0095AE09 CALL 0x00878350, then the epilogue at 0095AE0E-0095AE1D with no MOV AL, so AL is the callee's. 00878350's body 00878350-0087839A is a four-case switch on byte [msg+10h] returning 1 for 4Bh/4Ch/56h/D2h and 0 by default. The pre-existing ledger record for 0095ABE0 already said "the default to the base handler 00878350", so the dispatch doc contradicted a record already in config/names/00950000.jsonl.

corrections.was: Kinds with a real target are `4Bh`, `4Ch`, ... ; every other index selects target `1Ah` = `0082237B`, the base call.
corrections.is: true as far as it goes, but three of the 27 targets do no unit work and the difference between them matters. Target 00h (4Bh, arm 00821EEA) calls the base and then forces AL to 1, discarding the base's answer. Target 01h (4Ch, arm 00821ED5) is the shared return-true epilogue and never reaches the base at all. Only target 1Ah (0082237B) returns the base's value. So 4Ch is swallowed by the unit rather than handled by it.
corrections.evidence: 00821EEA PUSH ESI / CALL 0095ABE0 / 00821EF1 MOV AL,1 versus 0082237B PUSH ESI / CALL 0095ABE0 / 00822381 MOV ECX,[ESP+20h] with no MOV AL. The byte table at 00822400 gives index 00h to offset 0 and index 01h to offset 1, and the target dwords at 00822394 are 00821EEA and 00821ED5.

corrections.is: the arm entry for 4Bh is 00821EEA; 00821EEB is the CALL instruction inside it. The 99h and 9Ah rows are correct.
corrections.evidence: target dword index 00h at 00822394 is 00821EEA, and the instruction at 00821EEA is PUSH ESI with the CALL at 00821EEB.

corrections.was: the producers of 7Ah, 7Dh, 91h, 92h, 95h and 9Dh were attributed to 0080F750, 009531A0, 00814390, 0074E9C0, 0080FD90 and 009D6550
corrections.is: all six attributions were artefacts of resolving the containing function by nearest function start in local/bsp_index.sqlite, which has no end_address column. The six construction sites lie past the end of those functions, in code Ghidra has no function for. Four of the kinds have a second, verified site elsewhere; 91h's producer is the virtual at 008144A0 and 9Dh's is 009D6650, neither a Ghidra function.

open_questions: 6Ch MT_SHIP_SET_ENGINEJAMFAILURE and 98h MT_SHIP_WRECKED have no `PUSH <kind>` construction site. Their producers build the kind in a register, so finding them needs a data-flow pass over the 25 unattributable 0075B430 call sites rather than an immediate scan.

The vtable owners behind slots 144h, 208h, 220h, 224h, 238h and 2Ch were not resolved to functions: the six shared unit vtables would each have to be read at those displacements. 220h/224h in particular are the whole of the five SET/CLEAR failure kinds.
00819A20 (kamikaze) and 0074E860 (leak zone load) are covered only at their heads; both are on the armed path and would repay a full read.
0093AA90's middle argument (msg+24h) is passed through to the point-effect creation but its use was not isolated.

00953F60 and 00954000 filter devices on the descriptor kind word at device+3F4h+80h with the sets {1,5,6} and {2,3,4,6}. Which device classes those numbers are was not established, so the two walkers are named by their sets rather than by a device name.
No run-time evidence: the harness does not load a mission, so none of these arms was observed executing.
tool_problems: `bsp.py ghidra xrefs` under-reports the kind immediates, as the packet brief warned, so every producer here comes from a byte scan of the PE's .text rather than from Ghidra references.

The index database at local/bsp_index.sqlite has no end_address column, so a containing-function lookup had to fall back to the nearest function start at or below the site. Every row cited in host_steps and producer_steps was re-checked by tools/verify_report_calls.py, which uses the live bodies.
`bsp.py ghidra export <addr> --asm` is not a valid flag combination; the assembly listing comes from `bsp.py ghidra export` followed by `bsp.py show <addr> --asm`.
Ghidra's decompiler dropped the second stack argument of 0074F440 and the ECX of 008141A0, 009540D0 and 00954170; the argument counts came from the RET imm and the listing instead.
limitations: Ghidra was not modified. Names recorded in the ledger are hypotheses except the MT_* kind literals, which are image strings.
Coverage is per-routine in the `routines` block; two callees are partial and say which range was read.
The producer classification answers 'can the image build this kind locally', not 'does a given mission build it'. A Lua binding existing does not prove any shipped mission script calls it.

producer_steps_in_undefined_code.why: These six 0075B430 construction sites lie in code Ghidra has no function for, so tools/verify_report_calls.py rule 2 cannot bind them to a caller. Each site's routine was bounded from the disk bytes instead (see no_ghidra_function). Four of the six kinds also have a second site inside a defined function, which is the row kept in producer_steps; 91h and 9Dh do not.
